name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Ablative Shroud Mk. IV
product_name: Arcturus Defense Solutions Ablative Shroud Mk. IV
description:
The Ablative Shroud Mk. IV is Arcturus Defense Solutions' fourth-generation ablative coating system, designed as a modular over-armor layer that can be applied to existing body armor or worn as a standalone protective garment. It consists of 64 individually bonded ceramic-aerogel tiles arranged in overlapping scales across a flexible carbon-weave backing. Each tile is designed to fracture and ablate in a controlled pattern upon ballistic or directed-energy impact, dissipating kinetic energy laterally across neighboring tiles and venting thermal energy outward rather than inward. A single tile failure does not compromise the structural integrity of adjacent tiles, giving the Shroud exceptional multi-hit performance before requiring field replacement.

The Mk. IV iteration introduced Arcturus's Fracture-Mapping HUD integration, a thin sensor filament woven through the backing layer that reports real-time tile integrity to any compatible tactical display. This allows the wearer and their team to monitor armor degradation in the field and prioritize tile replacement during pauses in engagement. Replacement tile cartridges — standardized 4x4 packs — are widely available through Arcturus supply chains and several third-party manufacturers, making the Shroud one of the most maintainable armor systems in the GLMZ market.

The Shroud is visually distinctive: its overlapping tile pattern gives it a scaled, almost organic appearance, and the fractured tiles left after engagement create a scarred, asymmetric texture that many operators choose not to replace immediately, wearing the damage as a record of engagements survived. Military contractors, mercenary units operating in high-threat zones, and certain well-funded resistance cells all field the Mk. IV, though the cost of replacement tiles is a persistent logistical burden.

specifications.coverage: Full torso, upper legs, upper arms (modular)
specifications.impact_resistance_rating: NIJ Level III+ equivalent per fresh tile
specifications.directed_energy_attenuation: Up to 85% thermal dissipation on first strike
specifications.hud_integration: Compatible with Arcturus Parallax Threat Lattice and third-party displays

tactical_use: The Shroud's tile-by-tile degradation model encourages operators to rotate their profile during sustained fire, presenting fresh tile sections to incoming rounds. Teams using Fracture-Mapping HUD integration can relay armor status to a squad leader, who can pull heavily degraded operators from the front line. The Shroud performs especially well against burst-fire engagements and directed-energy weapons, which tend to concentrate thermal load — the ablative geometry handles concentrated energy better than distributed ballistic loads.
cultural_context: Among mercenary units, the condition of a soldier's Shroud tiles is a form of social currency — a fully intact Shroud means you're either new or haven't seen real action, while a heavily scarred set of tiles means you've been in it. Some operators deliberately mismatched tile colors or left cracked tiles in place as a form of personal iconography. Arcturus has tried to capitalize on this by releasing 'Veteran Finish' pre-scarred tiles, which the actual mercenary community largely regards with contempt.
known_users: Sergeant Dava Orel (retired ADS field tester, now freelance)
story_hooks: A third-party replacement tile manufacturer has begun selling counterfeit cartridges that look identical to Arcturus originals but fail catastrophically on second impact — operators are dying in the field.
An Arcturus logistics depot holding six months of tile inventory has been seized by an unknown faction, creating a critical supply shortage among contracted units who depend on the Shroud.

The Fracture-Mapping sensor filaments have been found to transmit low-bandwidth location data to Arcturus servers — the company claims it's for 'performance analytics,' but the data granularity suggests active surveillance.
A decommissioned Mk. IV Shroud recovered from a crime scene shows tile fracture patterns that forensic analysts claim are inconsistent with any known weapon system — something new is in the field.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, scale-like armor overlay with 64 ceramic-aerogel tiles arranged in overlapping rows across the torso and limbs. The tiles create an almost reptilian aesthetic, with sharp geometric edges that catch light distinctly. Fresh tiles gleam with a faint iridescent sheen; worn tiles appear chalky and fractured, creating a deliberately asymmetric, battle-scarred appearance.
physical_description.dimensions: Full torso coverage (approximately 60cm H × 45cm W), upper arm panels (25cm each), upper leg panels (35cm each). Modular tile system allows custom configuration.
physical_description.weight_description: 11.2 kg total — substantial but distributed across the body. Requires wearing over base layer or integrated into existing armor harness; typically worn as over-armor rather than standalone.
physical_description.primary_material: Ceramic-aerogel tiles bonded to flexible carbon-weave backing with reinforced stitching at seams. Tiles are composite ceramic-matrix composite with controlled fracture geometry.
physical_description.finish: Matte ceramic on tile surfaces with microstructured edge bevels for controlled fracturing. Carbon-weave backing has a subtle woven texture. Tiles show deliberate weathering and scuff marks from handling.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal-gray tiles with pale cream/ivory accents along tile edges where fracture patterns are engineered. Backing is gunmetal gray. Some units display operator customization: faded corporate insignia, hand-painted kill markers, or dye-stained patches.
physical_description.interface_elements: Thin sensor filament embedded in backing (visible as faint metallic threading along seams under close inspection). Four standardized cartridge slot ports on lower torso in matte black, each labeled with Arcturus logo. Small indicator ports for HUD feed integration at shoulder junction.
distinctive_features: Overlapping scale-tile pattern creates organic, almost predatory silhouette
Fractured and missing tiles on combat-worn examples create asymmetric damage maps
Faint iridescent sheen on fresh tiles that dulls after thermal cycling
Visible sensor filament threading along seams like surgical stitching
Cartridge slot ports with push-fit mechanical locking for field replacement
Subtle Arcturus Defense Solutions embossed logos at shoulder and hip points
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Arcturus Defense Solutions logo (geometric A within circle) embossed at both shoulders. 'ABLATIVE SHROUD MK. IV' stamped on lower torso backing in sans-serif font. Batch serial number and manufacturing date etched on reverse side. 'FRACTURE-MAPPING COMPATIBLE' label on sensor integration ports.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained units show minor scuffing on tile edges and carbon backing. Combat-worn examples feature multiple fractured or missing tiles creating an irregular surface texture, with replacement tiles often mismatched in color or wear stage. Sensor filament may show minor discoloration from thermal stress. Some operators deliberately leave damaged tiles unfilled for 24-48 hours to display battle readiness.
